title: OpenAI compat: deferential tool_choice handling and inline schema annotations for stable tool framing
author: Marina Lopez
body:
Context: As we continue to harden the OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling, we observed two classes of failure in production e2e tests and a customer incident: 1) models emitting partial tool-like payloads inline (e.g. a JSON blob inside assistant content) versus an explicit tool_choice; 2) downstream tooling mis-attributing nested or union-typed fields between OpenAI-style tool schemas and Redwood's canonical tool schemas.
Motivation: these cases cause fragile routing (sometimes invoking the wrong tool), streaming desynchronization, and noisy developer UX when SDKs surface both an assistant content chunk and a separate tool invocation for the same logical action.
Summary of changes:
- Implement "deferential tool_choice" semantics in the openai-compat dispatcher: when both assistant.content and a tool_choice/frame are present in the same turn, prefer the explicit tool_choice but synthesize an "assistant.action" frame that preserves assistant prose for backward compatibility. This prevents double-invocations while keeping streaming clients informed.
- Introduce inline schema annotations inside tool frames (a lightweight "@rw_schema" hint) to bridge OpenAI union/nullable patterns to Redwood's strict tool schemas. The annotation is optional at runtime and ignored by downstream tools that don't understand it.
- Add an escape/frame marker for tool outputs emitted in-stream so that the streaming parser never re-interprets tool output as fresh tool_choice suggestions (fixes stream-looping). Implemented as a sentinel chunk type and a small change to the framing protocol so existing clients are still forward-compatible.
- SDK surface updates (TS/Python): expose a new field on streaming events: openai_compat_meta.tool_decision with reason and confidence score when available. This makes client-side routing/logging easier and helps SRE debugging.
- Tests & docs: new e2e integration test for mixed assistant+tool payloads, unit tests for schema annotation parsing, and a doc page describing recommended usage and compatibility caveats.
Checklist:
- [x] Runtime dispatcher changes
- [x] Streaming frame marker and parser updates
- [x] Schema annotation parser and validator
- [x] SDK event surface updates (TS, Python)
- [x] Tests (unit + e2e)
- [x] Documentation (openai-compat/tool-deferential.md)
- [x] Telemetry: emit a metric openai.compat.tool_choice.deferred_count on defer events
Migration notes: none required for most customers; customers relying on raw assistant content may need to inspect the new assistant.action frame if they previously parsed assistant.content for tool invocation. See docs for examples.
commits: feat(openai-compat): deferential tool_choice arbitration and assistant.action synthesize
feat(streaming): add TEv:TOOL_FRAME_ESCAPE sentinel and parser changes
chore(sdk): expose openai_compat_meta.tool_decision on streaming events
test: add e2e mixed payload test and unit schema annotation tests
review_comments: Jordan Kim: The deferential rule makes sense; please add a short comment in dispatcher.rs explaining why assistant.action is synthesized (for future maintainers).
Marina Lopez: Added in latest commit and expanded comment to include a small example of prior broken behavior.
Priya Shah: Can we ensure the TEv:TOOL_FRAME_ESCAPE sentinel is idempotent for clients that don't understand it? I don't want older clients to drop frames.
Marina Lopez: Yes — escape marker is emitted as a typed chunk and older clients will ignore unknown chunk types; added unit test to assert no-op for legacy parser.
Evan Rivers: Unit tests look good. One nit: schema annotation uses '@rw_schema' key — consider namespacing to avoid collisions (e.g., '@rw.schema'). Not a blocker.
Marina Lopez: Renamed to '@rw.schema' and updated docs and parse logic to support both legacy variations for a short deprecation window.
release_notes: Adds deferential arbitration when assistant content and tool_choice both appear; introduces optional inline '@rw.schema' annotations in tool frames; streaming safety marker to avoid re-parsing tool outputs; SDK event augmentation exposing tool decision metadata.
notes_for_release: Behavioral change only in arbitration ordering (explicit tool_choice preferred).
No customer action required unless you parse assistant.content for tool dispatching; see migration doc.
